sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].

The window is not a straight line: growth stepped up to 17.5% in FY2021 and 15.8% in FY2022, then fell back to 6.8% in FY2023 and 5.0% in FY2024 before re-accelerating to 10.1% in FY2026 [D189][D238][D287][D336][D434].
The FY2021 jump came from comparable sales up 16%, with e-commerce comparable sales up 44%, plus gasoline and currency tailwinds [P54][P55][P56].
FY2022 growth was driven by a 14% comparable sales increase and $14.8 billion of warehouse ancillary sales, strongest in gasoline, business centers and travel [P42].
The U.S. segment supplied +7.2pp of FY2026's 10.1% revenue growth on a 72.5% share, with Other International adding +1.6pp and Canada +1.3pp [D672][D670][D679][D686][D434].
Net sales rose $27.3 billion, or 10%, on comparable sales up 8% (5% average ticket, 3% frequency) plus 25 net new warehouses [P14].
Operating income grew 12.5% against revenue growth of 10.1%, an incremental operating margin of 4.7% [D435][D434][D457].
Operating costs grew 0.1pp slower than revenue in FY2026, with cost of revenue up 10.2% and SG&A up 8.9% [D458][D449][D450].
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% against net income growth of 13.9% as the diluted share count fell 0.1% to 444.4 million [D438][D436][D452][X100].
Operating margin of 3.9% in FY2026 sits at the window high, above the 3.4% median and the 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp, with SG&A adding +0.1pp and cost of revenue flat at -0.0pp [D447][D460][D459].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though excluding gasoline price inflation it rose one basis point, with currency adding $126 million [P9].
In FY2026 net margin of 3.0% sat 0.8pp below the 3.9% operating margin, a gap of 0.8pp [F52][F32][D732].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income in FY2026, above the 1.75x window median and the 1.26x low [F82][F42][D421][D722][D721].
The increase was primarily due to higher operating income and reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow of $9.4 billion was a 3.1% margin, above the 2.8% median, with capex at 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A [F102][D418][D698][D417][D423].
Investing outflow rose to $6.4 billion, primarily capital expenditures [P5][F112].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, in the 100th percentile of four retail peers against a -18.3% median [D427][D428][D733][D734].
Cash and investments rose 39.4% to $21.3 billion while total debt grew 6.5% to $6.2 billion [D453][D425][D454][D426].
Buybacks plus dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow, with $848 million of repurchases and $2.5 billion of dividends [D429][D430][X110][X120].
Financing outflow of $3.4 billion mainly reflected dividends, repurchases and debt repayments [P4][F122].

Operating margin of 3.9% ranks in the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, and net margin of 3.0% also sits at the 17th percentile against 3.5% [F32][D709][D710][F52][D711][D712].
The thin-margin model is structural rather than deteriorating, since the margin is at its window high and has widened steadily from 3.2% in FY2017 [F23][F32].
Free cash flow margin of 3.1% is only at the 50th percentile against a 4.2% peer median despite the strong net cash position [D418][D713][D714].
Cash generation is adequate but not differentiated, so the balance-sheet cushion rather than cash margin is the durable advantage.
Whether operating margin holds at or above the 3.9% FY2026 high, or slips toward the 3.4% median, in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D691][D692].
Whether free cash flow margin stays above the 2.8% median or falls toward the 1.5% FY2022 low, in the FY2027 cash flow statement [D418][D698][D696].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue holds above the 5.0% FY2026 level or reverses toward the 2.1% FY2024 reading, in the FY2027 balance sheet [D428][D330].
